title: Debug: Customers Who Never Ordered — Sometimes Empty, Sometimes Not
description:
This query is supposed to list every customer who has never placed an order. It works on some data, but on other data it mysteriously returns **zero rows even though customers who never ordered clearly exist**. Find the bug and fix it.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
hint: If even one row in the NOT IN subquery is NULL, the whole NOT IN comparison becomes unknown for every single row — silently emptying the result. NOT EXISTS never has this problem, because it only ever checks for matching rows, not list membership.
outputExplanation: On the Example data (no NULLs), both the buggy and fixed queries agree: Henry and Max never ordered, so both come back. The trap only shows up on the hidden "NULL order" case — three customers, one order with a `NULL` customer_id. There, `id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM shop_orders)` compares every customer's id against a list that contains a NULL. Since `id = NULL` is neither true nor false but *unknown*, and `NOT IN` needs every comparison in the list to definitively fail, a single NULL in the subquery poisons the whole check — the buggy query returns **zero rows** even though real never-ordered customers exist. `NOT EXISTS` never has this problem: it just checks row-by-row for a match, so a stray NULL customer_id is simply one more order that doesn't match — harmless.

tests.name: Example — no NULLs yet, bug isn't visible here
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO shop_customers VALUES (1,'Joe'),(2,'Henry'),(3,'Sam'),(4,'Max');
INSERT INTO shop_orders VALUES (1,3),(2,1);

tests.name: Every customer has ordered
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO shop_customers VALUES (1,'Joe'),(2,'Henry');
INSERT INTO shop_orders VALUES (1,1),(2,2);

tests.name: One NULL order alongside real never-ordered customers — the trap
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO shop_customers VALUES (1,'Joe'),(2,'Henry'),(3,'Sam');
INSERT INTO shop_orders VALUES (1,1),(2,NULL);

tests.name: NULL order present, but everyone has actually ordered
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO shop_customers VALUES (1,'Joe'),(2,'Henry');
INSERT INTO shop_orders VALUES (1,1),(2,2),(3,NULL);

tests.name: Multiple NULL customer_id rows in orders
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO shop_customers VALUES (1,'Joe'),(2,'Henry'),(3,'Sam');
INSERT INTO shop_orders VALUES (1,NULL),(2,NULL),(3,1);

tests.name: Duplicate customer names, mixed ordering
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO shop_customers VALUES (1,'Alex'),(2,'Alex'),(3,'Ravi');
INSERT INTO shop_orders VALUES (1,3),(2,NULL);

tests.name: Larger mixed set with a NULL order thrown in
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO shop_customers VALUES (1,'A'),(2,'B'),(3,'C'),(4,'D'),(5,'E'),(6,'F');
INSERT INTO shop_orders VALUES (1,2),(2,2),(3,4),(4,6),(5,NULL);
